takeaway: Lymph from the abdominal oesophagus drains to the gastric and coeliac nodes; the upper two-thirds drain upwards; the wall is inner circular, outer longitudinal.

lines.text: Which statement about the anatomy of the oesophagus is true?
Follow the oesophagus down through the diaphragm into the abdomen.
Lymph from its abdominal portion usually drains into the gastric
and coeliac lymph nodes. That is the true statement.
Higher up, the upper two-thirds usually drain upwards: cervical to internal jugular nodes, thoracic to mediastinal nodes.
And watch the trap: the wall has inner circular and outer longitudinal muscle, not the other way round.
lines.say: (laugh) And watch the trap: the wall has inner circular and outer longitudinal muscle, not the other way round.

lines.text: So the answer: abdominal oesophageal lymph drains to the gastric and coeliac nodes.
